title: Mixed methods investigation of treatment expectations in a psychosomatic inpatient treatment setting
summary:
Patients' expectations of medical or psychotherapeutic treatment often play a role in the success of these treatments. Since these expectations can be influenced, for example, in conversations between practitioners and patients, they are a potential lever for improving therapies. To do this, however, we need to better understand in which diseases treatment expectations play an important role. 
We would like to investigate this in the field of psychosomatic medicine in patients with anorexia nervosa. This patient group suffers from particularly high disstress, and many patients experience a relapse even after inpatient treatment. It is therefore important to continuously improve therapeutic methods. 
In our study, we compare expectations of patients with anorexia nervosa with those of others who are starting inpatient psychosomatic therapy. In addition, we analyse associations between prior experiences and expectations. In our mixed methods approach, we combine questionnaires handed out to a larger sample of people with different diagnoses and interviews conducted with a smaller sample of people with anorexia nervosa. Using semi-structured interviews, patients are asked about their expectations at the beginning and end of their inpatient treatment. The interviews allow us to focus on the perspective of those affected. At the same time, the questionnaires enable us to look specifically at changes in expectations.

interventions.name: Patients with a range of diagnoses, who fill in quantitative surveys during their psychosomatic inpatient treatment.
Patients with anorexia nervosa (F50.0) or atypical anorexia nervosa (F50.1), who fill in quantitative surveys and participate in qualitative interviews during their psychosomatic inpatient treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Inpatient treatment in the clinic for psychosomatic medicine and psychotherapy
- Inclusion criterion for interview sub-study: diagnosis F50.0 or F50.1
Exclusion criteria:
- Persons with insufficient knowledge of German or a severe psychiatric or somatic comorbidity that significantly hampers study participation as assessed by the study coordinator
